articles.title: Four Bihar districts most heatwave-prone: Centre - The Times of India
articles.full_text: Four Bihar districts most heatwave-prone: Centre According to climate sensitivity and seasonal weather monitoring reports of the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the four districts in southwestern Bihar are particularly vulnerable to extreme heat. Dehri in Rohtas has been identified among the areas consistently reporting high maximum temperatures. The minister said the Bihar Meteorological Service Centre has installed Automatic Weather Stations (AWS) in all blocks of the state to strengthen weather and climate services and provide localised early warnings. The system is aimed at enabling communities, citizens and institutions to take timely measures during extreme weather events and strengthen local climate adaptation planning. Bihar has also prepared a State Action Plan on Climate Change (SAPCC) in line with the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC), which provides a broader framework for climate-related action across the country. The Union environment ministry has provided financial assistance to Bihar for preparation of the SAPCC, while the Ministry of Science and Technology has established a State Climate Change Cell (SCCC) in Bihar under the National Mission on Strategic Knowledge for Climate Change. The minister said district-level studies are also being undertaken under the programme. articles.title: Prohibition has brought social change in Bihar, says JD(U) minister - The Times of India
articles.full_text:
Prohibition has brought social change in Bihar, says JD(U) minister
Her assertion came amid calls from some NDA allies for a review of the policy. Since the budget session of the state legislature earlier this year, MLAs of NDA partners, prominently Madhav Anand of the Rashtriya Lok Morcha led by Rajya Sabha member Upendra Kushwaha, have called for a graded review of the policy.
The demand has since moved from a review of the policy to calls for introducing the Gujarat model of prohibition, which was first enforced in 1949 and amended in 2017. Union minister and former CM Jitan Ram Manjhi has backed the Gujarat model during a visit to Patna. Earlier, Manjhi had also favoured a review of the policy.
Meanwhile, social and macroeconomic experts associated with the National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER) have called for lifting the ban on the manufacture, sale, storage, transportation, trade and consumption of liquor in Bihar. The NCAER findings were made public last week.
In its report, presented at the India Policy Forum 2026, NCAER argued that the prohibition policy had not resulted in a decline in violence against women and that women’s safety had not improved significantly.
The report also said the excise department contributed 14% of the state’s revenue for three consecutive financial years before prohibition was imposed, suggesting that the ban had resulted in a loss of revenue for the state.
Despite the criticism of the policy, Mandal defended the govt’s position on Tuesday. “Earnings of the poor and middle classes are being spent on the education of their children and for the overall happiness of their families,” she said, adding that prohibition had led to a “reduction in violence against women, increase in family savings, sense of security among women and social harmony.”

articles.title: All registration offices to go paperless by Aug 17 in Bihar - The Times of India
articles.full_text:
All registration offices to go paperless by Aug 17 in Bihar
Naveen said the home registration facility, earlier available to senior citizens aged 80 and above through mobile registration units, had been extended to those aged 75 and above for flat and land registration.
He asked service providers to ensure necessary assistance and convenience to the public during paperless document registration. Their remuneration has been fixed at Rs1,000 for documents valued up to Rs1 lakh, Rs2,500 for documents valued between Rs1 lakh and Rs5 lakhs and Rs5,000 for documents valued above Rs5 lakh.
The secretary also called for an online public grievance module to make the process more effective and transparent.
Naveen asked all assistant inspector generals to conduct regular site inspections of registration offices to boost revenue collection and curb revenue evasion. He told officials to ensure GIS-based inspections and communicate the instructions to all district registration offices.
He stressed effective action against rule violations and revenue evasion to protect revenue interests. He also asked officials to expedite pending recovery proceedings related to auctions, prioritising major cases while ensuring speedy disposal of smaller cases as per rules.

articles.title: PK promises 10k private jobs for Bankipur youths, improved education and welfare delivery - The Times of India
articles.full_text:
PK promises 10k private jobs for Bankipur youths, improved education and welfare delivery
Kishor also announced plans to facilitate private-sector jobs for 10,000 youths within a year, promised improvements in education and welfare delivery, and said issues related to the Rs 1,100 pension and foodgrain entitlements would be addressed on priority.
“Ever since the Bankipur election result came out, Bihar is no longer talking about encounters. Every day, the discussion is about education and employment. That is the power of your vote,” he said, taking a dig at CM Samrat Choudhary during meetings across the constituency.
Addressing residents, Kishor said many people had been asking about his whereabouts since the election result. “I have been working on exactly that,” he said before announcing an employment initiative for local youths. “If your child is educated, submit their resume. We will ensure jobs for at least 10,000 youngsters from here,” he said, adding that he had reached out to contacts across the country to create opportunities for people from Bihar.
“If any assembly constituency in Bihar gets the highest number of jobs, it will be Bankipur,” he added, expressing confidence that young people would not have to migrate outside the state for work under a future Jan Suraj-led system.
On welfare delivery, Kishor promised visible improvements within three months. He said no one would have to pay bribes for ration cards and urged senior citizens not receiving the Rs 1,100 pension to approach his office.
On education, Kishor said people’s lives would change only through better schooling and employment opportunities. He claimed that within a year either govt schools would improve significantly or children would be able to study in private schools without their families bearing the cost of fees.
Kishor also linked the Bankipur verdict to recent action in the Bharat Tiwari firing case, saying an awakened electorate had forced political leaders to shift their attention towards education and employment.
Kishor attended a remembrance and condolence meeting in Dashratha before holding thanksgiving programmes in Yarpur Rajputana, Jakkanpur and Langartoli as part of his Aabhar Yatra.

articles.title: Proposed Patliputra township to have 651-acre sports hub - The Times of India
articles.full_text:
Proposed Patliputra township to have 651-acre sports hub
Mishra said the govt was focusing on creating modern sports infrastructure to help Bihar’s youth develop their talent and compete at national and international levels. “Patliputra township will become a centre of world-class sports facilities,” he said, adding that the initiative was part of efforts to provide athletes with better facilities for training, practice and competition.
According to the integrated plan for the township, around 225 acres will be earmarked for the Sports City, while 187 acres will be developed as a golf course and another 239 acres as a modern sports complex.
The proposed Sports City will include advanced facilities for different sporting disciplines, along with infrastructure required for training and competitions. The sports complex will provide facilities for a wide range of sporting activities, giving residents as well as athletes access to modern amenities.
Sports minister Shreyasi Singh said the township should be developed as a future-ready urban centre equipped not only with modern civic facilities but also with high-quality sports infrastructure. She said the proposed facilities would be developed in line with Olympic standards, enabling Bihar to host national and international sporting events and providing its athletes with opportunities for world-class training and competition.
Shreyasi also said land required for sports facilities would be identified in all 12 proposed townships across the state. The objective is to ensure that each township has adequate and quality sports infrastructure, she added.

articles.title: Woman, daughter killed by train in West Champaran - The Times of India
articles.full_text:
Woman, daughter killed by train in West Champaran
Family said Janki had gone to a grocery shop with her daughter. While returning home, they were hit by the 63341 Muzaffarpur-Narkatiaganj MEMU train.
Narkatiaganj RPF post commander Rituraj Kashyap and Shikarpur police reached the spot and sent the bodies for postmortem.
Shikarpur SHO Manoj Kumar Singh said, “Sofwa village is divided into two parts by the railway track. People generally cross the tracks to move from one side to the other. The woman was returning home with her daughter after purchasing grocery items when they were hit by the train.”
